about: An invented island group. No model has seen these facts, so a report can only get them right by reading the sources.

docs.title: Brenna Isles
docs.text: The Brenna Isles are a group of three inhabited islands in the Corran Sea: Halvey, Ostra and Little Mar. The largest island is Halvey, home to about 4,200 people. The isles have been governed by the Brenna Council since 1923. The council meets in the town of Port Seld on Halvey. Most residents work in fishing, sheep farming or the ferry trade.

docs.title: Port Seld
docs.text: Port Seld is the main town of Halvey and the seat of the Brenna Council. Its harbour was rebuilt in 1958 after a storm destroyed the old stone pier. The Seld Lighthouse stands at the harbour mouth. Port Seld hosts the Wool Fair every September. The town's school was founded by the teacher Agnes Corrie in 1887.

docs.title: Seld Lighthouse
docs.text: The Seld Lighthouse was built in 1871 by the engineer Thomas Varga. It is 31 metres tall and its light can be seen 22 nautical miles away. The light was automated in 1979, and the last keeper, Ruth Ellam, retired that year. The lighthouse is now run by the Corran Lights Trust.

docs.title: Thomas Varga
docs.text: Thomas Varga (1832-1904) was a civil engineer born in Aberlin. He designed four lighthouses in the Corran Sea, including the Seld Lighthouse. Varga also built the swing bridge at Mardale in 1866. He trained under the engineer Helen Ashdown before opening his own office in 1860.

docs.title: Halvey Ferry Company
docs.text: The Halvey Ferry Company runs boats between Port Seld, Ostra and the mainland port of Kessick. It was founded in 1902 by the brothers Owen and Peter Lusk. The company's largest ship, the MV Corran Star, entered service in 2011 and carries 340 passengers. Crossings from Port Seld to Kessick take about two hours and ten minutes.

docs.title: Ostra
docs.text: Ostra is the second-largest of the Brenna Isles, with about 900 residents. Its only village is Tarrin, where the Ostra Cheese Cooperative is based. Ostra has no airport; visitors arrive on the Halvey Ferry Company's boats. The island's standing stones, known as the Nine Maidens, date from around 2500 BC.

docs.title: Ostra Cheese Cooperative
docs.text: The Ostra Cheese Cooperative was set up in 1964 by twelve farming families in Tarrin. Its best-known cheese is Tarrin Blue, a sheep's-milk blue cheese aged for at least ten weeks. The cooperative won a gold medal at the Kessick Food Awards in 2019. It sells most of its cheese at the Wool Fair in Port Seld and through shops on the mainland.

docs.title: Little Mar
docs.text: Little Mar is the smallest inhabited island of the Brenna Isles, with 46 residents. It is known for its puffin colony of about 3,000 breeding pairs. A small chapel on the island was restored in 1998 with money raised by the Corran Lights Trust. Little Mar can only be reached by a private boat from Ostra.

docs.title: Brenna Council
docs.text: The Brenna Council was created in 1923 to govern the three inhabited Brenna Isles. It has nine elected members who serve four-year terms. The council's first chair was Margaret Lusk, the daughter of the ferry founder Owen Lusk. The council meets in the Old Customs House in Port Seld.

docs.title: Corran Lights Trust
docs.text: The Corran Lights Trust is a charity founded in 1981 to look after historic lighthouses in the Corran Sea. It took over the Seld Lighthouse in 1983. The trust's director since 2015 has been Daniel Okafor. Besides lighthouses, the trust has funded the restoration of the chapel on Little Mar.

docs.title: Wool Fair
docs.text: The Wool Fair is held every September in Port Seld. It began in 1908 as a market for Halvey sheep farmers. Today it draws around 6,000 visitors, most of whom arrive on the Halvey Ferry Company's boats. The fair's main prize, the Brenna Fleece, is awarded for the best raw wool.

docs.title: Kessick
docs.text: Kessick is a mainland port town on the Corran Sea coast. It is the mainland terminal for the Halvey Ferry Company. Kessick hosts the annual Kessick Food Awards, which began in 1995. The town has a railway station with trains to the city of Aberlin.

docs.title: Ruth Ellam
docs.text: Ruth Ellam (1921-2007) was the last keeper of the Seld Lighthouse. She served at the light for 31 years, from 1948 until it was automated in 1979. After retiring she wrote a memoir called The Long Watch, published in 1986. She was born on Ostra, in the village of Tarrin.

docs.title: Agnes Corrie
docs.text: Agnes Corrie (1851-1930) was a teacher who founded the school in Port Seld in 1887. She was born in Kessick and moved to Halvey in 1880. Corrie also campaigned for the creation of the Brenna Council. A street in Port Seld, Corrie Lane, is named after her.
